content:
You don't say whether you let it 'restart to update'. Did you? Have you rebooted the computer? Does Thunderbird otherwise work as it should?

If the answer to all those is Yes, I'd blame the symptoms on a botched upgrade. I'd try the following (make a backup copy of your Thunderbird Profile first; see <https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/thunderbird-export> for how to do that):

- Download the installer for the same version from <https://www.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/all/> and install it over the current installation.

- If that doesn't improve the situation I'd uninstall the current version, reboot the computer, then reinstall Thunderbird.

content:
You must have a password in order to access Yahoo's email servers. If you have lost or forgotten it, you can reset it on the Yahoo web site.

As you download the Thunderbird installer from the official site, <https://www.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/all/> you will be presented with a request for a donation. The request can be dismissed with the [X] in the upper right corner of the web page, but it doesn't matter because, the installer file will still continue to download. If you have downloaded the Windows installer, you should look for a file named "Thunderbird Setup 159.0.exe" or similar, maybe in your Downloads folder. You must run that file in order to install Thunderbird.
